sentences.zh: 平心而论，对这些经理来说，他们确实在试图完成一项艰巨的挑战，那就是把办公室变成一个目的地。

sentences.en: to participate in them as it's kind of dutiful and maybe not exactly where they would choose to spend their 5 to 6.30 p.m.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: after work, but they're playing ball.
sentences.zh: 员工去那里是因为他们在做工作，而且公司要求他们在那里。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，他们的老板看着他们说：“嗯，我们可不仅仅是要你来这儿干活。”

sentences.en: And to be fair to these managers, I mean, they are trying to do a difficult challenge, which is make the office a destination.
sentences.zh: “我们要让这地方对你来说无比精彩。”

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And workers are going there because they're doing their jobs and they're required to be there.
sentences.zh: 对许多人来说，这本身就是一个有点复杂的命题，因为如果这是工作，那它就不是目的地。

sentences.en: And meanwhile, their bosses are looking at them and saying, well, we're not just going to have you come here and do your jobs.
sentences.zh: 它是一份工作。

sentences.en: We're going to make this so exciting for you.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Which is in and of itself a somewhat complicated proposition for many people because if it's work, then it's not a destination.
sentences.zh: 懂了。

sentences.en: It's a job.
sentences.zh: 原来如此。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没问题。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 明白。

sentences.en: What else are companies doing in this moment to make this work?
sentences.zh: 为了促使员工回办公室上班，公司目前还在采取什么其他举措？

sentences.en: You know, I've also seen a lot of companies that are actually rethinking what the office has to physically look like if it's a destination.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我还看到很多公司实际上在重新思考，如果办公室要成为一个目的地，它在物理上应该长成什么样。

sentences.en: And I think about this as sort of like the living roomification of the office.
sentences.zh: 我把这看作是办公室的“客厅化”。

sentences.en: If you're going to get your workers to leave home, then you want to make the office maybe look a little bit more like their homes.
sentences.zh: 如果你想让员工离开家，那你就会希望办公室看起来更像他们的家一点。

sentences.en: And I've talked with some of the biggest office designers in the world.
sentences.zh: 我采访过一些全球顶尖的办公室设计专家。

sentences.en: I've talked with companies that supply office furniture.
sentences.zh: 我采访过提供办公家具的公司。

sentences.en: And I've visited a lot of offices that have physically remade themselves to look like more of a place where you might want to spend time.
sentences.zh: 我还参观了许多重新装修过的办公室，它们在物理上改造了自己，变得更像一个你愿意消磨时间的地方。

sentences.en: One of the funniest ones I visited was actually a cereal making company.
sentences.zh: 我参观过的最有趣的地方之一，实际上是一家麦片制造公司。

sentences.en: And this is a kind of buzzy, very Instagram friendly cereal company.
sentences.zh: 这是一家很有人气、非常适合发到Instagram上的麦片公司。

sentences.en: And they decided to make their office look like a cereal box.
sentences.zh: 他们决定把办公室装扮成一个麦片盒的样子。

sentences.en: Why not?
sentences.zh: 为什么不呢？

sentences.en: Why not?
sentences.zh: 为什么不呢？

sentences.en: What does it look like when your office resembles a cereal box?
sentences.zh: 当你的办公室酷似一个麦片盒时，它是什么样子的？

sentences.en: I mean, there was a little bit of me that was like, I could live here.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我内心有那么一瞬间觉得：我能住在这里。

sentences.en: And they told me their motto is to be a Froot Loop in a world of Cheerios.
sentences.zh: 他们告诉我，他们的座右铭是在全麦圈的世界里做一个彩虹圈。

sentences.en: And so they're trying to bring that into every piece of furniture in the office.
sentences.zh: 所以他们正努力把这一点融入办公室的每一件家具中。

sentences.en: There are bright pink couches and planters everywhere.
sentences.zh: 到处都是亮粉色的沙发和花盆。

sentences.en: They really leaned into the fake plants.
sentences.zh: 他们真的很喜欢那些假植物。

sentences.en: They sourced a lot of their furniture vintage.
sentences.zh: 他们采购了大量的复古家具。

sentences.en: It's color everywhere.
sentences.zh: 到处都是色彩。

sentences.en: It's a little bit psychedelic feeling.
sentences.zh: 感觉有点迷幻。

sentences.en: I also visited, you know, an office that really feels like stepping into like a Soho club, like it's very hotel lobby.
sentences.zh: 我还参观了一个办公室，那种感觉就像是走进了苏荷区的俱乐部，非常像酒店大堂。

sentences.en: There was really chic, curated collections of books.
sentences.zh: 那里有非常别致、精心挑选的藏书。

sentences.en: There was like little nooks where you have armchairs, lots of upholstery, you know, faux grapes, Keith Haring coffee table books.
sentences.zh: 还有一些放着单人沙发的小角落，大量的软包家具，你知道的，还有假葡萄、凯斯·哈林的咖啡桌读物。

sentences.en: It really feels like you are stepping in somewhere special.
sentences.zh: 这真让人感觉你走进了某个特别的地方。

sentences.en: So it looks very glamorous.
sentences.zh: 所以它看起来非常有魅力。

sentences.en: I think the actual experience of working there is not the easieSt.
sentences.zh: 我觉得在那里工作的实际体验并不轻松。

sentences.en: It's not always the most conducive to working.
sentences.zh: 它并不总是最利于工作。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: What a lot of workers tell me is that, you know, a game night or a bar cart can be fun here and there.
sentences.zh: 很多员工告诉我，你知道的，偶尔搞个游戏之夜或推个酒吧手推车可能会挺有趣。

sentences.en: But there's also a cringiness.
sentences.zh: 但这也带有一种尴尬感。

sentences.en: To some of these efforts, there's also the challenge of it makes getting your job done at the office a little bit harder.
sentences.zh: 对于其中一些举措，同时也面临着这样一个挑战：这会让在办公室完成工作变得稍微困难了一点。

sentences.en: And then there's the fact that when you look at the numbers, they haven't really budged.
sentences.zh: 然后还有一个事实是，当你查看数据时，它们并没有真正发生动摇。

sentences.en: So HR managers are kind of throwing the kitchen sink at this problem of getting people back in the office.
sentences.zh: 因此，人力资源经理们可以说是绞尽脑汁来解决让员工回到办公室这个问题。

sentences.en: But is it really doing all that much?
sentences.zh: 但这真的起多大作用吗？

sentences.en: There's numerical evidence you're saying that ultimately this isn't really moving the needle all that much.
sentences.zh: 你是说，有数字证据表明，这最终并没有真正起到多大作用？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: From the numbers on how full offices actually are, things have really plateaued.
sentences.zh: 从办公室实际满员率的数据来看，情况确实已经进入了平台期。

sentences.en: And finally, there are companies that are actually doing sticks, not carrots.
sentences.zh: 最后，有些公司实际上在采取强硬手段，而不是温和的胡萝卜政策。

sentences.en: And what do those sticks look like?
sentences.zh: 那些强硬手段是什么样的？

sentences.en: I mean, for some companies, that looks like basically turning back the clock to pre-pandemic
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，对某些公司来说，这基本上就像是把时钟拨回大流行之前

sentences.en: and saying, we will see you at your desk five days a week, nine to five or nine to nine.
sentences.zh: 然后说，我们每周有五天在办公桌前见，朝九晚五或是朝九晚九。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Give us some examples of that.
sentences.zh: 给我们举几个这方面的例子吧。

sentences.en: I'm really curious what that looks like and what the response from workers is.
sentences.zh: 我真的很想知道那是什么样的，以及员工们的反应如何。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, I've talked to an AI company outside San Francisco, for example, where the CEO is adamant that people have to be in five days a week.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我采访过旧金山郊外的一家人工智能公司，那里的首席执行官坚决认为人们必须一周来办公室五天。

sentences.en: What he said to me is that, you know, none of the greatest inventions in history were made on Zoom.
sentences.zh: 他对我说的是，你知道的，历史上最伟大的发明都不是在Zoom上诞生的。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: It's possible that, you know, we just haven't seen the greatest Zoom invention yet.
sentences.zh: 有可能，你知道的，我们只是还没看到最伟大的Zoom发明诞生罢了。

sentences.en: But his thought is that they are doing very difficult, very fast moving work in artificial intelligence.
sentences.zh: 但他的想法是，他们在人工智能领域从事的是非常困难、节奏极快的工作。

sentences.en: It is a highly compensated job.
sentences.zh: 这是一份薪酬很高的高薪工作。

sentences.en: And it's an exciting place to work because you're surrounded by really smart people.
sentences.zh: 这也是一个令人兴奋的工作场所，因为你的周围都是非常聪明的人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so he will not make any exceptions to the idea that he wants to see everyone in the office five days a week.
sentences.zh: 因此，他绝不会破例，他希望看到每个人每周五天都在办公室。

sentences.en: He tells me he has the fullest parking lot in the Bay Area.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我，他拥有湾区最满的停车场。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: I'm curious if this stick approach ever backfires.
sentences.zh: 我很想知道这种强硬的方法是否会适得其反。

sentences.en: It definitely does.
sentences.zh: 绝对会的。

sentences.en: You know, some companies have taken a much harder line approach to return to office and they've lost people over it.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，有些公司对重返办公室采取了更为强硬的态度，结果因此失去了员工。

sentences.en: Grindr, the gay dating app, is a good example of that.
sentences.zh: 同性恋约会应用Grindr就是一个很好的例子。

sentences.en: They decided this summer that they wanted people back in the office at least a couple of days a week.
sentences.zh: 他们今年夏天决定，希望员工每周至少有几天回到办公室上班。

sentences.en: But they wanted people back in the same offices as their teams and managers.
sentences.zh: 但他们希望员工回到与他们的团队和经办经理相同的办公室。

sentences.en: And Grindr had grown during the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 而且Grindr在大流行期间一直在发展壮大。

sentences.en: They'd hired people who had come on with the understanding that they would just be working from home for as long as they wanted.
sentences.zh: 他们招募了一些员工，这些员工进来时达成的共识是，只要他们愿意，就可以一直在家工作。

sentences.en: From wherever they were.
sentences.zh: 无论他们在哪里。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And then the company said they were going to have to relocate cities to report to the same offices as their teaMs.
sentences.zh: 然后公司却说他们必须重新搬迁城市，以便去和团队相同的办公室报到。

sentences.en: And Grindr did lose some people over that policy.
sentences.zh: Grindr确实因为这项政策失去了一些员工。

sentences.en: There were people who just left the company because they decided they did not want to move cities to, you know, report to the office a couple of days a week.
sentences.zh: 有些人直接离开了公司，因为他们决定不想为了每周去办公室报到几天而搬迁城市。

sentences.en: On the other hand, the management was really firm that they think that the company is going to do much better and the work is going to be stronger if people are near their teams
sentences.zh: 另一方面，管理层态度非常坚定，他们认为，如果人们在物理上靠近他们的团队，

sentences.en: physically and if they can interact with their managers, getting that feedback, building those relationships.
sentences.zh: 并且如果他们能与经理互动、获得反馈、建立这些关系，公司就会做得更好，工作也会更出色。

sentences.en: And as you've been talking here, it's occurred to me that the absolutists in the return to office debate that we now know is over, they might have had a point.
sentences.zh: 正如你刚才所说，我突然意识到，我们现在都知道已经结束的“重返办公室”辩论中的极端主义者，他们可能也有他们的道理。

sentences.en: And let me just explain.
sentences.zh: 让我解释一下。

sentences.en: Their point was basically that workers should either all be in the office five days a week or they should be allowed to work from home whenever they want.
sentences.zh: 他们的观点基本上是，员工要么应该全部每周五天都在办公室，要么应该被允许随时在家工作。

sentences.en: And that way, there's not this hybrid split brain problem of uncertainty, anxiety, forced fun.
sentences.zh: 这样一来，就不会出现这种充满不确定性、焦虑感和强行娱乐的混合分裂大脑问题。

sentences.en: You know, the workers who are in the office all the time, they get the benefit of the connection,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，那些一直呆在办公室里的员工，他们获得了人际连接、

sentences.en: predictability, clear sense of professional development and the corporate ladder where they're headed.
sentences.zh: 可预测性、清晰的职业发展感以及他们前进的职场晋升阶梯带来的好处。

sentences.en: And those who work from home all the time get the clear benefits of being truly remote.
sentences.zh: 而那些一直远程办公的人则获得了作为真正的远程办公人员的明显好处。

sentences.en: They don't have to commute.
sentences.zh: 他们不必通勤。

sentences.en: They don't end up going to the office like you do in a booth on a Zoom call.
sentences.zh: 他们不会像你一样，最终跑进隔间里开Zoom会议。

sentences.en: And instead of either of those, what we have is this kind of muddled compromise that is now a kind of permanent reality.
sentences.zh: 与其选择其中任何一个，我们得到的却是一种糊里糊涂的妥协，而这现在已经变成了一种永久的现实。

sentences.en: Well, I think a lot of people are hopeful that we can get to a place where hybrid is the best of both worlds.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为很多人都抱着希望，希望我们能达到这样一种状态：混合办公能够兼顾两者的优势。

sentences.en: I think, you know, people were given a level of flexibility during remote work that is just hard to take back from them.
sentences.zh: 我想，你知道的，远程工作期间给予人们的那种灵活性是很难再收回的。

sentences.en: I think, you know, what a lot of researchers I've spoken to have said is that when they look at studies on the effects of remote work on productivity, they're kind of all over
sentences.zh: 我想，你知道的，我交谈过的许多研究人员都表示，当他们查看关于远程工作对生产力影响的研究时，这些研究结果简直

sentences.en: the map.
sentences.zh: 五花八门。

sentences.en: And the reason is that it basically comes down to how well managed those hybrid work plans are.
sentences.zh: 原因在于，这基本上取决于这些混合办公计划的管理水平有多高。

sentences.en: When they're done well, it makes people more productive.
sentences.zh: 如果管理得当，它会让人更有生产力。

sentences.en: When they're done badly, it makes people less productive.
sentences.zh: 如果管理不善，它会让人生产力下降。

sentences.en: And so I think, you know, we've suddenly arrived at the end of the return to office battles.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，你知道的，我们突然迎来了重返办公室之争的终点。

sentences.en: And now everyone's trying to figure out how do we make this reality actually work for people.
sentences.zh: 现在每个人都在试图弄清楚，我们如何才能让这种现实真正为人们所用。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it's not just about, you know, some coder wearing headphones on a beanbag in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是关于，你知道的，某个穿着连帽衫、坐在旧金山懒人沙发上戴着耳机的程序员。

sentences.en: It's about people across so many industries, across so many parts of the country.
sentences.zh: 这关乎各行各业、全国各地许许多多的人。

sentences.en: Like, this is a phenomenon, again, touching tens of millions of people.
sentences.zh: 就像这是一个再次触及数千万人的现象。

sentences.en: And people are really trying to figure out how do we make this work in a way that doesn't feel cringy and, you know, counterproductive.
sentences.zh: 人们真的在试图弄清楚，如何以一种不会让人觉得尴尬且适得其反的方式来促成这一切。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it feels reasonable to remember that it took decades and generations to build up the previous system and then very little time to essentially break it down and arrive at
sentences.zh: 而且记住这一点是合乎情理的：建立之前的系统花了几十年甚至几代人的时间，而将其彻底打破并演变成

sentences.en: this new hybrid model and therefore stands to reason that it's going to take years and years, maybe decades, to come up with a true replacement, a set of structures, rituals
sentences.zh: 这种新的混合模式却只花了很短的时间，因此不难推断，要想找到一个真正能替代它的方案，建立起一套围绕混合办公的结构、仪式

sentences.en: and rhythms around hybrid work that are going to make it better, more sustainable, less cringy.
sentences.zh: 和节奏，让它变得更好、更可持续、不那么尴尬，将需要长年累月，甚至几十年的时间。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: I mean, I think the workplace has seen huge changes before.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为职场以前经历过巨大的变革。

sentences.en: We've seen the entrance of women into the workplace.
sentences.zh: 我们见证了女性进入职场。

sentences.en: We've seen personal computers, which meant you could do your work wherever, whenever.
sentences.zh: 我们见证了个人电脑的出现，这意味着你可以在任何地方、任何时间工作。

sentences.en: But I can't think of another time when the workplace has changed fundamentally overnight.
sentences.zh: 但我记不起还有哪个时期，职场会在一夜之间发生根本性的改变。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You know, we woke up one morning and suddenly had to work in an entirely different way in a different place, just remake our routines.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们某天醒来，突然就不得不以完全不同的方式、在不同的地方工作，只能重新建立我们的日常习惯。

sentences.en: And so I think it stands to reason that it's going to take more than a couple of years to really figure out how to make that actually work for people.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，不难推断，要真正弄清楚如何让这一点切实为人们所用，需要的时间绝对不止几年。

sentences.en: And hybrid work also is a new chapter.
sentences.zh: 而且混合办公也是一个新的篇章。

sentences.en: You know, we sort of got used to remote work.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们有点习惯了远程办公。

sentences.en: We got used to logging into Zoom and slacking with people and sending them emojis as a way to bond, but we haven't really totally gotten to a comfortable place with hybrid yet.
sentences.zh: 我们习惯了登录Zoom、在Slack上和别人交流、发表情符号作为建立联系的方式，但我们还没有完全在一个让混合办公感到舒适的状态。

sentences.en: We're still figuring out, is it the bar cards?
sentences.zh: 我们仍在琢磨：是靠酒吧手推车吗？

sentences.en: Is it the game nights?
sentences.zh: 是靠游戏之夜吗？

sentences.en: Is it the sticks?
sentences.zh: 是靠强硬手段吗？

sentences.en: Like, what's going to make this actually effective so that people don't commute and then lock themselves in a, you know, hermetically sealed room?
sentences.zh: 究竟是什么才能让这一切真正奏效，从而不至于让人们通勤赶来，结果却把自己关在一个，你知道的，严密密封的房间里？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, you have brought me to my final question, which is, what is it going to take to get you, Emma, out of that booth?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你把我引向了我的最后一个问题，那就是：究竟要怎样才能把你——艾玛——从那个隔间里请出来？

sentences.en: Have you thought about that?
sentences.zh: 你考虑过这个问题吗？

sentences.en: Well, you know, I'm here with you right now, having a great time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道的，我现在正和你在一起，玩得很开心。

sentences.en: You have left your booth for us.
sentences.zh: 你为了我们已经离开了你的隔间。

sentences.en: I've left my booth for you guys, and sometimes my co-workers bring in really good snacks.
sentences.zh: 为了你们我确实离开了隔间，而且有时我的同事会带很好吃的零食来。

sentences.en: That's what gets you out.
sentences.zh: 这就是把你吸引出来的东西。

sentences.en: That draws me out.
sentences.zh: 这把我吸引了出去。

sentences.en: But I also think, you know, everyone's kind of finding their own comfortable resting place.
sentences.zh: 但我也认为，你知道的，每个人都在寻找自己舒适的休憩之所。

sentences.en: The booth is working for me.
sentences.zh: 这个隔间对我来说挺合适的。

sentences.en: I would recommend it.
sentences.zh: 我很推荐它。

sentences.en: You know, you can pop in and out.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你可以随时进出。

sentences.en: You can still have lunch with your co-workers.
sentences.zh: 你依然可以和同事一起吃午饭。

sentences.en: You can bump into your manager.
sentences.zh: 你可以偶遇你的经理。

sentences.en: Everyone's finding that sort of resting place that works for them.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在寻找适合自己的那种休憩之所。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: One day at a time, we're feeling it out.
sentences.zh: 过一天算一天，我们正在慢慢摸索。

sentences.en: Well, Emma, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，艾玛，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们真的很感激。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me on.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来参加。

sentences.en: In person.
sentences.zh: 当面交流。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: On Wednesday, pressure intensified on former South Carolina Governor Nikki Haley to drop out of the Republican presidential race and coalesce around Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 周三，前南卡罗来纳州州长妮基·黑利面临的压力越来越大，人们敦促她退出共和党总统竞选，并团结在唐纳德·特朗普周围。

sentences.en: With the Republican Party's chairwoman, Ronald McDaniel, telling Fox News that Haley has no shot at winning.
sentences.zh: 共和党全国委员会主席罗娜·麦克丹尼尔在接受福克斯新闻采访时表示，黑利没有获胜的可能。

sentences.en: I think she's run a great campaign, but I do think there is a message that's coming out from the voters, which is very clear.
sentences.zh: 我认为她开展了一场伟大的竞选，但我确实认为选民们传递出的信息非常明确。

sentences.en: We need to unite around our eventual nominee, which is going to be Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 我们需要团结在我们最终的提名人周围，也就是唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: Haley has vowed to stay in the race.
sentences.zh: 黑利已誓言将继续参选。

sentences.en: And one of her biggest supporters, New Hampshire Governor Chris Sununu, forcefully rejected McDaniel's call for Haley to end her campaign.
sentences.zh: 她的主要支持者之一、新罕布什尔州州长克里斯·苏努努强力拒绝了麦克丹尼尔关于黑利结束竞选的呼吁。

sentences.en: With all due respect to Ronald McDaniel, to say that we're just going to call it after two states, 40 states to go.
sentences.zh: 出于对罗娜·麦克丹尼尔的尊重，仅仅因为比了两个州就说我们要收兵了，后面还有40个州呢。

sentences.en: The head of the Republican Party saying we don't want to hear from all the other Republicans in the nation.
sentences.zh: 共和党领袖说我们不想听取全国其他所有共和党人的意见。

sentences.en: That's nonsense.
sentences.zh: 这简直是无稽之谈。

sentences.en: You've got to let the voters decide, not a bunch of political elites out of D.C.
sentences.zh: 你必须让选民来决定，而不是由华盛顿的一群政治精英来决定。

sentences.zh: 他们是全黑睡眠者吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是不是喝到断片才去睡觉。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们对光线有什么要求？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一种非常具体的情况。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢喝咖啡还是茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
